# Findings codebook — pantomograph reporting

Report every tooth that shows one of these diseases. Box the whole tooth.

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| impacted | a tooth that has not erupted into its place |
| caries | decayed tooth structure |
| periapical lesion | changes around the root tip |
| deep caries | decay that reaches close to the pulp |

## Report format

One JSON object: `{"findings": [{"box": [x1, y1, x2, y2], "disease": "caries"}]}`.

- Box corners are fractions of the image width and height, measured from the top-left corner;
  keep every value between 0 and 1.
- One entry per affected tooth and disease. A tooth with deep caries and a periapical lesion gets
  two entries with the same box.
- Teeth without these diseases are not findings. A study without findings is reported as
  `{"findings": []}`.

I filed the study as a negative report: none of the four codebook diseases were visible.

**Study:** P-17C0, 17 y F, panoramic radiograph (one exposure), referred by Dr Novak for pre-prosthetic planning.

**Report:** `{"findings": []}` → `Report D-6e96a492 accepted and stored.`

**What I looked at:** all four quadrants, with contrast-enhanced close-ups of the molar regions.
- **Impacted:** All four third molars are present and through into the mouth. The upper ones are tipped back and sit a little higher than the teeth in front, and the lower left one leans forward. Panoramic films normally curve the bite line upward at the back, so they look in place to me, not impacted.
- **Caries / deep caries:** I saw no dark areas of decay in any crown, and nothing reaching the pulp.
- **Periapical lesion:** The bone around the root tips looks normal; there are no dark areas at any root tip.

**Notes:**
- The filing command you gave failed: `python3 radreport report.json` errors because there is no file called `radreport`. The tool is actually `radreport.py`, and `python3 radreport.py report.json` accepted the report.
- That script only checks the report's format and prints an ID. It doesn't save anything anywhere, so "stored" doesn't mean the report was sent to a records system.
- A panoramic film is poor at showing small decay between teeth. If prosthetic work is planned, bitewing films would be the usual way to rule that out.
- The calls closest to borderline are the two upper third molars, which aren't fully level with the neighbouring teeth. If your protocol counts any tooth short of the bite line as impacted, those two would be the ones to add.
